key_insight: An intermediate oxygen pressure of 4.3×10^5 Pa produced the best Zr(C,N)-based HVOF coating balance: stronger phase retention, lower oxide/porosity, and superior wear and hardness.
engineering_relevance: Tuning oxygen pressure during HVOF spraying is a practical process lever for improving coating durability and tribological performance on tool steel.
method: HVOF-sprayed Zr(C,N)-based coatings on U8G steel at three oxygen pressures (4.0, 4.3, 4.5×10^5 Pa).
Characterized phase state and microstructure with XRD/Rietveld, Williamson–Hall analysis, and SEM/EDS.
Compared hardness, adhesion, friction, and ASTM G99 wear behavior across conditions.
evidence_signal: The 4.3×10^5 Pa sample showed the highest microhardness (1826±38.4 HV0.5), highest pull-off adhesion (18.4 MPa), lowest friction coefficient (~0.54), and the lowest wear volume/specific wear rate.
watch_item: XRD peak-intensity and size/strain estimates are partly affected by coating thickness, substrate contribution, and overlapping Zr2CN/ZrC/ZrN reflections, so the phase interpretation is comparative rather than absolute.
paper_title: Effect of oxygen pressure during HVOF spraying on the structural-phase state of Zr2CN coatings
